items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Bob Thomas' solo on 'Bourbon Street Parade' as something the interviewer's dad used to teach them; INTERVIEWEE does not claim personal interaction with Bob Thomas.

ctx.x: So I mean to learn melodies, which I don’t think we accentuate upon them enough in the schools. I mean my dad had recorded a record with Paul Barbarin in the 1950s and one of the cuts on there was “Bourbon Street Parade” which Paul Barbarin wrote. And what my dad used to do was he’d tell us “I’m going out for a while, and I want you to learn like Bob Thomas’ solo on ‘Bourbon Street Parade.’” And as a result of that I can hum that solo right now, you know? That had that kind of impact on me. And you know I mean…
